title: Relative length of DVR lattices equals determinant valuation
statement: Let $R$ be a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], let $K$ be its fraction field, and let $V$ be a finite-dimensional $K$-vector space [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace]. Let $M\subseteq V$ be an $R$-submodule which is finitely generated [def-weil-finitely-generated-module] and whose $K$-linear span is $V$. Let $g:V\to V$ be a $K$-linear isomorphism and put $H=M\cap g(M)$. Write $\ell_R$ for module length [def-weil-pbc-module-length], $\det_K(g)$ for the endomorphism determinant [def-weil-endomorphism-determinant], and $v_R:K^\times\to\mathbf Z$ for the normalized valuation, defined by $v_R(ut^r)=r$ for a unit $u\in R^\times$, a uniformizer $t$ and $r\in\mathbf Z$. Then both $M/H$ and $g(M)/H$ have finite $R$-length, and, regarding those lengths as integers, $$\ell_R(M/H)-\ell_R(g(M)/H)=v_R(\det_K(g)).$$

source.place: Tag 02MI (lemma-order-vanishing-determinant), specialized to a DVR, with the finite-length assertion from Tag 02MF (lemma-compare-lattices) and the distance definition Tag 02MG (definition-distance). Order as defined in Tag 02MD (definition-ord) is the normalized uniformizer exponent for a DVR.
